abstract: Querying the Sequence Read Archive traditionally relied on submitter metadata that is often missing, inconsistent, or wrong. Logan changed that picture by assembling the archive for direct sequence searches with kmindex and LexicMap. Yet hits are not alignments. Variation and uneven coverage fragment genes across assembly pieces, while redundant outbreak isolates overwhelm comparative evolutionary tools. We built disassembler to reconstruct complete coding sequences from unitig graphs or contigs, thin clonal duplicates, and build deep cohorts spanning up to millions of runs. From 4.99 million SARS-CoV-2 hits, disassembler recovered 910,848 strict and 1,153,319 permissive Spike sequences. Paired with the Aeon tools (HyphAeon, RhizAeon, and ChronAeon), downsampled cohorts ([≤] 200 haplotypes) resolve evolutionary dynamics in seconds without iterative tree search. Across SARS-CoV-2, microbiome obelisks, and Helicobacter pylori, panels recover a 2.55-fold Omicron clock acceleration, gyrA drug-pocket rigidity, oipA/vacA/Spike co-selection, 57.4% mixed obelisk infections with six mosaic tracts, and 5.37-fold vacA recombination enrichment.
